mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate directly increases the cost of capital for corporations, reducing the present value of future cash flows and leading to lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 3.5%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a strengthening labor market and robust consumer demand, which together predict positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in UNRATE and increase in HOUST does not produce positive returns in more than 60% of cases over 60 days, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by annualized GDP growth above 2.5% and year-over-year CPI inflation above 3.0%), the S&P 500 is expected to underperform due to the heightened risk of Federal Reserve policy tightening and reduced corporate profit margins.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%), the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in total nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 5-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between PAYEMS and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index base 2017=100) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 100, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and a healthy economy, which together predict positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce positive returns in more than 60% of cases over 20 days, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (defined by the federal funds rate above 4.0% and year-over-year CPI inflation above 3.5%), the S&P 500 is expected to experience negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to the contractionary impact on corporate borrowing and consumer spending.
failure_condition: In the monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%), the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
